profile.reading:
This is Telia's Helsinki Data Center, known in this registry and in industry usage by the shorthand Telia HDC, located at Valimotie 5 in the Pitajanmaki district of west Helsinki, Finland. The building opened in 2018 and was developed under the local project company Kiinteisto Oy Pitajanmaen Data Central, a name that appears, tied explicitly to TeliaSonera Finland Oyj, in a City of Helsinki permit decision dated January 3, 2017, authorizing a retaining wall between a sheet pile wall and the property line at Valimotie 3-5. That municipal record is a genuine primary confirmation that the City of Helsinki processed permitting for this specific site under Telia's corporate name, though the decision itself concerns a minor structural element tied to street level infrastructure, not the building's electrical or mechanical systems.

Telia Finland is the Finnish operating arm of Telia Company, headquartered in Solna, Sweden, and traces its roots to Sonera, Finland's former state telecommunications monopoly, which merged with Sweden's Telia in 2002 to form TeliaSonera, later renamed Telia Company in 2016. This is worth distinguishing clearly from the other Finnish facility in this registry, Hetzner HEL1 in Tuusula. Telia is a national telecom operator building a data center as an extension of its carrier and enterprise services business, marketing this site for high density enterprise and hyperscale colocation with heavy emphasis on liquid cooling for AI and GPU workloads. Hetzner, by contrast, is a German budget focused hosting and cloud server company whose Finnish campus is built around dense, standardized colocation for its own retail and business hosting customers rather than bespoke enterprise deployments. Same country, same broad category of facility, different business model entirely.

On scale and power, Telia's own technical documentation and the engineering firm Ramboll, which held the project management and construction oversight role for the build, both describe the facility as built out to 24 megawatts of IT capacity, with Ramboll's own project page additionally citing 110 kV power line coordination as part of its scope, indicating the site draws from a high voltage grid connection substantially larger than typical distribution voltage, though Ramboll does not state a separate utility contracted capacity figure in megawatts distinct from the 24 MW IT number. No standby generation or onsite generation figure in megawatts was found from any source consulted this session. Ramboll's figures put the building at roughly 34,000 square meters and 241,550 cubic meters, with a first phase investment of approximately 150 million euros and construction running 2016 to 2018.

The facility recovers waste heat for the City of Helsinki's district heating network, a detail consistent with the Finnish capital's broader efforts to secure grid capacity for data centers only where waste heat can be captured, since Fingrid, Finland's transmission system operator, has separately stated it cannot connect new consumers over 10 megawatts to its backbone grid across large parts of southern Finland, including the Helsinki metropolitan area, until roughly 2027, a constraint driven by lost generation capacity as older Helsinki area power plants close and by a surge of agreed data center and battery storage connection requests nationally. No source consulted this session ties that Fingrid constraint to Telia HDC specifically, since the facility predates the current bottleneck by several years, but it is directly relevant regulatory context for any further expansion at this site. Helsinki's own city planning office has separately processed a zoning case for a Pitajanmaki electrical substation in the same district, case number 12805, indicating the area carries dedicated grid infrastructure, though this record was not confirmed to serve this specific building.

What remains unconfirmed is a facility specific utility contracted power figure distinct from the 24 MW IT number, any standby or onsite generation capacity, and the exact number of named tenants using the site.

The prior research_note referencing a Nasertic changelog entry could not be verified against any system this session had access to and was not carried forward. it_capacity_mw of 24 retained, now corroborated by Ramboll rather than only by an aggregator. No utility, standby, or onsite generation MW figure confirmed.
